title: The door's claude-sub step-down is refused by the Go executor's model check
description:
A rung dispatch with no free subscription makes the door answer the stepped-down Workers AI pair (claudeSubLeaseForBoot's designed fallback, tick 6fv: 'no worker ever queues on a subscription'), but the Go client refuses any handle whose model is not the one its dispatch resolved — pinned by TestAHandleBootedOnAnotherModelIsRefused as 'a door that fell back to its own default is refused'. The two designs cancel out: a claude-configured run whose subscription is busy cannot fall back to Workers AI for its workers at all — every dispatch is answered with the stepped-down handle and refused client-side, and the reconciler burns the attempt's retries re-asking until a subscription frees. The review boot's step-down works (the Workflow composes its own boot); the worker dispatch's does not. Either the client admits the step-down (the handle already names what ran), or the door answers a typed no-subscription refusal the orchestrator can wait on.
evidence: cloudflare/src/sandbox-executor.ts:1825 (claudeSubLeaseForBoot steps the pair down), cloudflare/test/sandbox-dispatch.test.ts:488 (the door answers pi-durable/glm for a claude/sonnet ask), internal/exec/cloudflaresandbox/executor.go:445 (the client refuses the model the dispatch did not resolve)
